answer: Imagine a harbor where each ship must moor at its own jetty, paying one solid anchor as bond — an anchor no captain can split, rent, or run in parallel. A hollow hull with no anchor is turned away; the haven shelters only ships that paid the iron's weight. One captain dividing his gold across ten hulls buys ten anchors at a tenth weight each, and since voice grows with the square of the bond, his ten voices together carry a tenth of one honest ship's. Ten clones, ten anchors, a tenth of the say.
